title: QNu Labs and NIELIT Partner on Quantum Technology Training in India
html:
Insider Brief

  • QNu Labs and the National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT) have signed an MoU to expand quantum technology education, technical training and workforce development in India.
  • The proposed collaboration includes industry-oriented curricula, practical training, faculty development, certification programmes and the potential establishment of Quantum Labs through a Hub-and-Spoke model.
  • The organisations will also explore hackathons, internships, on-the-job training and industry engagement to prepare students and professionals for roles in quantum technologies and quantum-safe cybersecurity.

PRESS RELEASE — QNu Labs (www.qnulabs.com), a global leader in end-to-end hybrid quantum cybersecurity solutions, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT), an autonomous scientific society under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), to strengthen quantum technology education, skill development and capacity building in India.

The collaboration aims to bridge the gap between emerging technology requirements and industry-ready skills by bringing together QNu Labs’ experience in quantum technologies and NIELIT’s institutional network and expertise in technical education and training.

Under the proposed areas of collaboration, the two organisations will work towards developing learning and training programmes in quantum technologies, including quantum-safe cybersecurity. The partnership will also explore the establishment of Quantum Labs at mutually identified institutions through a Hub-and-Spoke model, alongside the development of industry-oriented curricula, learning resources and practical training opportunities.

The initiative will further focus on hands-on learning through demonstrations, projects and hackathons, faculty development and Train-the-Trainer programmes, assessment and certification, as well as opportunities for industry interaction, internships and on-the-job training, wherever feasible and mutually agreed upon.

Commenting on the collaboration, Rahil Patel, Chief Growth Officer, QNu Labs, said, “The next phase of the quantum revolution will not be defined by technological breakthroughs alone, but by how effectively nations build the capabilities to translate them into real-world applications. For India, this calls for a deeper integration of industry expertise, academic institutions and specialised skill development. As quantum technologies begin to reshape the future of cybersecurity and digital infrastructure, preparing a workforce that understands both the science and its practical applications becomes increasingly important. Our association with NIELIT is an opportunity to contribute to this larger ecosystem-building effort and strengthen the foundations for India’s quantum-ready future.”

Dr Madan Mohan Tripathi, Director General, NIELIT, said, “As emerging technologies reshape the global technology landscape, the ability to build specialised competencies will be central to India’s long-term technological progress. Quantum technology, in particular, requires a strong foundation of scientific understanding, applied learning and industry-relevant skills. Through our association with QNu Labs, we seek to strengthen the interface between technical education and industry requirements, creating greater opportunities for hands-on learning and capacity building. Such collaborations are important in ensuring that our talent ecosystem evolves in step with the technologies shaping the future.”

The collaboration reflects a shared focus on strengthening India’s capabilities in quantum technologies by connecting industry expertise with institutional learning. By fostering practical skills, specialised training and greater industry-academia engagement, the initiative aims to contribute to a talent ecosystem equipped to support India’s evolving quantum technology landscape.
